title: Loss Functions & Optimization Landscapes
description: Quantify model error with MSE, MAE, Binary Cross-Entropy, and Categorical Cross-Entropy across complex non-convex surfaces.

slides.title: Measuring Model Error 🎯
slides.content:
# Loss Functions & Optimization Landscapes

A **Loss Function** $\mathcal{L}(\hat{y}, y)$ quantifies the mathematical penalty when model prediction $\hat{y}$ deviates from ground truth $y$.

Training a neural network is mathematically formulated as an optimization problem: discovering weight parameter values $\mathbf{w}^*$ that minimize total loss across the training distribution:

$$\mathbf{w}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{w}} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathcal{L}(f(\mathbf{x}_i; \mathbf{w}), y_i)$$

slides.title: Selecting the Right Loss Function 📋
slides.content:
# Common Loss Functions in Modern AI

| Learning Task | Loss Function | Mathematical Formulation | Output Layer Activation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Regression (Standard)** | Mean Squared Error (MSE) | $\frac{1}{N} \sum (y - \hat{y})^2$ | Linear (Identity) |
| **Regression (Outlier-Robust)**| Mean Absolute Error (MAE) | $\frac{1}{N} \sum \|y - \hat{y}\|$ | Linear (Identity) |
| **Binary Classification** | Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) | $-\frac{1}{N} \sum [y \ln \hat{y} + (1-y)\ln(1-\hat{y})]$ | Sigmoid |
| **Multi-Class Classification**| Categorical Cross-Entropy | $-\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i} \sum_{k} y_{ik} \ln \hat{y}_{ik}$ | Softmax |

Cross-Entropy heavily penalizes confident wrong predictions: predicting $\hat{y} = 0.001$ when $y = 1$ incurs an astronomical loss ($-\ln(0.001) \approx 6.9$).

quizData.question: Which loss function should be paired with a Softmax output layer for classifying images into 10 mutually exclusive animal species?
quizData.explanation: Categorical Cross-Entropy paired with Softmax is the standard maximum likelihood formulation for multi-class classification.

slides.title: Computing Loss in PyTorch 🐍
slides.content: Evaluating Cross-Entropy and MSE loss in PyTorch:
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Multi-class loss (raw logits + target class index)
ce_loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
logits = torch.tensor([[1.5, 0.2, -0.8]]) # batch=1, classes=3
target = torch.tensor([0]) # correct class index is 0

loss_value = ce_loss(logits, target)
print('Cross-Entropy loss:', loss_value.item())

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Non-Convex Landscapes 💡
slides.content:
## Saddle Points vs Local Minima
Linear regression loss is a smooth convex bowl with a single global minimum. Deep neural network loss surfaces, however, are non-convex with billions of dimensions, containing saddle points and ravines.

Modern research proves that in high-dimensional spaces, optimization rarely gets trapped in bad local minima; rather, navigating flat saddle point plateaus is the primary training challenge!
